assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture and active sites underpins industrial refining, petrochemistry, emissions control and increasingly biomass conversion. Structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and hierarchical or tailored sites show clearly how structure determines function, and the structures were established by crystallographic work. The impact has been large, durable and measurable.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design and active-site engineering in industrial processes), Davis (new framework types and structure-direction rationale) and Zones (organic structure-directing agents, e.g. SSZ-13 for NOx control and hydrocracking) form a coherent three-person configuration. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis have strong claims but the field is broad, and the single discovery statement bundles synthesis, topology and catalysis.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and extensive commercial deployment make this mature. Timing is reasonable, though the 2025 MOF prize may make a framework-materials award feel close in time.
uncertainties: The candidate bundles several distinct advances, so the prize motivation would need a narrow focus (for example structure-directing synthesis for catalysis).
Priority between early zeolite pioneers and the design-era contributors is not settled by the supplied credit list.
As a structural chemist in this area I may overweight it; I rely on the supplied text and my background knowledge without independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase fixes N2 under ambient conditions, and atomic structures of the MoFe protein and its FeMo cofactor, including the interstitial carbide and the structural snapshots of CO and turnover-related states, turned a mystery into a structural-mechanistic problem. This is a fundamental structure-to-function story with links to the Haber-Bosch problem and to bioinorganic design.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the first MoFe protein crystal structures and later cofactor and ligand-bound states; Einsle resolved the central carbide and high-resolution structures; Seefeldt, with Dean and Hoffman, contributed the mechanistic framework. Ribbe and Dean are also strong, so assigning a maximum of three requires drawing a line between structural and mechanistic credit.
assessment.maturity: The structures are well confirmed by several groups. The overall catalytic mechanism, especially substrate binding and the order of electron and proton delivery, is still debated, so recognition would rest on the structural work rather than on a settled mechanism.
uncertainties: The mechanism of N2 reduction is unresolved, which may limit how much a motivation can claim.
Credit is split between structural biologists and spectroscopists/biochemists, with several excluded contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large new family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable surface terminations, high conductivity and applications in energy storage, electromagnetic shielding and catalysis. It is a clear materials-chemistry discovery with a defined origin in 2011 and a very rapid growth in the literature.
assessment.attribution: Naguib (first Ti3C2 synthesis, working with Gogotsi and Barsoum), Gogotsi and Barsoum form a natural three-person set, though the discovery is concentrated in a Drexel group and the roles are reasonably clear.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide with a large community and rising applications, but practical devices are not yet widespread, and structural characterization of terminations and disorder is still developing. The field is young relative to older candidates.
uncertainties: Surface terminations and local structure are only partially determined, which matters to me as a crystallographer.
Real-world application impact is still emerging, so the prize may be seen as slightly early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in a decade, linking defect chemistry, composition tuning and processing to device performance. The scientific and societal interest is exceptional, and the chemistry of composition and structure is central.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka (first perovskite-sensitized cell, 2009), Park (solid-state cells with stable high efficiency, 2012) and Snaith (meso-superstructured and planar devices, 2012) are the most defensible three; Seok, Grätzel and Kanatzidis also made decisive contributions, so the exclusion of strong people is a real concern.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are confirmed independently, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and manufacturing at scale are unresolved, and the Nobel standard of lasting impact may call for patience.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercial viability remain open, making recognition potentially premature.
Credit is crowded among at least six well-qualified people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-atom catalysts maximize atom efficiency and offer well-defined active sites that can be characterized by aberration-corrected electron microscopy and X-ray absorption, bridging homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis. The concept has led to a very large literature on reaction classes from CO oxidation to electrocatalysis.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Qiao, Wang, Zhang et al. Nature Chemistry paper coined the concept, with Jingyue Liu contributing key electron-microscopy evidence; Tao Zhang led the work. Datye and Li also contributed, and earlier related ideas on isolated sites make priority partly arguable.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing, but stability under real conditions and the rigor of site identification in many reports are uneven. As an electron-microscopy person I note that atomic-resolution images alone do not prove which sites are catalytically active.
uncertainties: Evidence that isolated atoms, rather than clusters or a minority of sites, drive activity varies by system.
Priority relative to older isolated-site catalysis is debatable, and the concept may be seen as incremental by some.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica (MCM-41 and related materials) extended molecular-sieve chemistry to the 2-50 nm range with tunable pore size, and spawned the field of ordered mesoporous solids. The materials are well characterized by diffraction and electron microscopy and influenced catalysis, adsorption and nanocasting.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil, MCM-41) have the clearest priority; Ryoo (carbon replicas, ordered mesoporous carbon, SBA-type syntheses) and Stucky/Zhao (SBA-15 and related) are major but make a crowded configuration. Related earlier Japanese work (FSM-16 by Inagaki) adds a priority question.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed, but industrial impact is more modest than for zeolites, and the peak of the field is past, which weakens the argument for recognition now.
uncertainties: Priority disputes between Mobil and Japanese groups.
Limited major practical application compared with zeolites.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved studies at room temperature before radiation damage, a methodological advance of the type that changes what a community can see. It is conceptually close to my own work on small crystals.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu proposed and championed the diffraction-before-destruction idea; Chapman led the first proof-of-principle experiments and method development; Schlichting led time-resolved applications; Fromme and others were also early leaders. The list contains several plausible subsets.
assessment.maturity: Proof of principle (2011) is well confirmed and growing, but the largest scientific payoffs, such as general time-resolved mechanisms, are still emerging, and access to XFELs is limited. Cryo-EM and microED compete for similar problems.
uncertainties: Hajdu's passing or current status should be considered, and I am uncertain of it.
Fit to the chemistry prize (versus physics or biology) may be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods made it possible to determine structures and probe dynamics of proteins beyond the size originally accessible, and the methods are used widely in structural biology and chemistry. Structure and dynamics information complements diffraction techniques for non-crystalline systems.
assessment.attribution: Clore and Bax (triple-resonance and residual dipolar coupling methods), Kay (relaxation dispersion and methyl-TROSY for large systems) and Gronenborn-type structural applications make strong claims; Palmer and Wagner are also strong, so the allocation is uncertain. Wuthrich was already recognized for NMR in 2002.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and heavily validated. The question is whether it is timely given the 2002 NMR prize and whether it counts as one coherent discovery.
uncertainties: The prior NMR prize reduces the margin for another NMR award.
The candidate covers many methods and the right focus is unclear.
